**Mechanism:**

1. For rows with access_count >= 10 and an access within seven days, raise priority by one only below the access ceiling of seven.
2. For stale rows within the access band, reduce by one to a floor of one; operator priorities 8–10 remain untouched. Return a before/after rollback entry and suppress mutation on dry-run.
3. The separate supersession-forgetting pass checks contradiction markers on both members and retains contested evidence rather than deleting the older row merely because a successor exists.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN.  Explicit eligible curator/autonomy cycle; --dry-run suppresses writes. These are deterministic passes, not independent model roles.

**Implementing symbols:** [src/mcp/stdio_guard.rs:254](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/stdio_guard.rs#L254) classify_fd; [src/mcp/stdio_guard.rs:271](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/stdio_guard.rs#L271) enforce_stdin_is_inherited_channel; [src/mcp/mod.rs:3384](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/mod.rs#L3384) dispatch_with_panic_isolation; [src/mcp/mod.rs:3404](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/mod.rs#L3404) handle_request; src/mcp/error_text.rs (typed rendering module).

**Mechanism:**

1. Inspect stdin’s descriptor type and refuse network/listening sockets or uninspectable channels; connected Unix sockets follow the explicit warning policy.
2. Parse line-delimited JSON-RPC and route named tools through a panic-isolated dispatch boundary with sanitized typed error rendering.
3. Bound oversized input handling and retain stable request ids/notification behavior so one handler panic does not intentionally terminate the whole process.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON.  Automatic on MCP startup/dispatch; profile_hint_in_errors controls optional profile hints. No streaming capability is advertised.

**Mechanism:**

1. Open bundled SQLite, initialize/migrate schema and set WAL, 5 s busy timeout and resolved synchronous/mmap pragmas.
2. WriteTxn owns BEGIN IMMEDIATE/deferred/exclusive boundaries with RAII rollback, reducing leaked transactions on errors.
3. SAL/read-pool paths attach read-only connections and use independent locks while retaining a serialized writer, so eligible reads need not hold the writer mutex.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON.  Default SQLite backend. AI_MEMORY_DB selects path; AI_MEMORY_DB_SYNCHRONOUS changes compiled NORMAL to a requested durability level; no remote server required.

#### F3-46 — Application-level peer replication with quorum writes and catch-up


**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · LOW (LOW 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Application-level peer replication with quorum writes and catch-up.

**Implementing symbols:** [src/federation/sync.rs:651](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L651) broadcast_store_quorum_with_embedding; [src/federation/sync.rs:913](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L913) broadcast_delete_quorum; [src/federation/sync.rs:1474](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L1474) broadcast_consolidate_quorum; [src/federation/sync.rs:1887](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L1887) broadcast_action_transition_quorum; [src/federation/sync.rs:2133](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L2133) broadcast_signal_create_quorum; [src/federation/sync.rs:2507](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L2507) bulk_catchup_push; [src/daemon_runtime.rs:8930](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/daemon_runtime.rs#L8930) sync_cycle_once.

**Mechanism:**

1. Commit locally, serialize signed federation operations and fan out to peers, collecting acknowledgements against the configured quorum and retaining failed deliveries for retry.
2. Catch-up push/pull advances per-peer cursors and merges accepted rows through backend admission; accepted inbox rows feed the local wake bus.
3. The same endpoint can remain a singleton or join multiple peers while using SQLite or a Postgres adapter; peers are application authorities, not merely database replicas.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN.  Configure federation peers/signing and run serve/sync workers; quorum_writes counts the local commit, so W=1 requires no remote acknowledgement. --catchup-interval-secs controls replay workers.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs:597](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs#L597)::sqlite_sync_push_applied_inbox_row_wakes_a_real_listener_3631; [tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs:643](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs#L643)::sqlite_catchup_applied_inbox_row_wakes_a_real_listener_3631; [tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs:713](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_inbox_wake_3631.rs#L713)::postgres_catchup_applied_inbox_row_wakes_a_real_listener_3631.

**Competitor finding:** 0. No equivalent established at this scope in the assessed source corpus. Competitors implement real replication, federation or Git synchronization, refuting broad 'only distributed memory' claims. No full signed, original-author-aware memory merge plus quorum and bounded catchup equivalent established. ai-memory's own convergence/cursor/resurrection defects make its integrated guarantee partial.

**Mechanism:**

1. List rows tagged recovered-from-transcript in the requested namespace or all non-internal namespaces; retain only Observation rows and consume a per-cycle classification budget (default 200).
2. Ask AutonomyLlm::classify_kind for a more specific kind; abstention/Observation is a no-op, and per-row errors are collected in the report rather than aborting the sweep.
3. Call MemoryStore::reclassify_memory_kind: protect existing Reflection/Persona kinds, increment row version and append a cause-bound signed audit event in the same transaction. Postgres locks the selected row FOR UPDATE.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN.  Cargo sal; curator --reflect with a real LLM and [curator].transcript_classify_enabled=true or AI_MEMORY_TRANSCRIPT_CLASSIFY_ENABLED=true. Default false; --dry-run suppresses reclassification writes.

**Competitor finding:** 6. TencentDB Agent Memory; OpenViking; Mem0 OSS; Cognee; iii/agentmemory; Redis Agent Memory Transcript classification into memory types is common extraction functionality. ai-memory's audited reclassification is optional and does not use a separately routed classifier or prove eventual processing of every candidate.

**Competitor code evidence:** [TC@90](#e-tc-90) ([source 1](https://github.com/TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory/blob/bd88cc83870bf9e7dbd2ec36aa13608d2295c7f4/MemoryCore/src/core/hooks/auto-capture.ts#L100-L160); [source 2](https://github.com/TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory/blob/bd88cc83870bf9e7dbd2ec36aa13608d2295c7f4/MemoryCore/src/utils/checkpoint.ts#L715-L753)); [OV@152](#e-ov-152) ([source 1](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/openviking/session/memory/extract_loop.py#L128-L158); [source 2](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/openviking/session/memory/extract_loop.py#L218-L256)); [MO@46](#e-mo-46) ([source 1](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/94c3fe9f238f3dbf29c9ce98643bd71eb13077cd/mem0/configs/base.py#L16); [source 2](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/94c3fe9f238f3dbf29c9ce98643bd71eb13077cd/mem0/memory/main.py#L760)); [COG@91](#e-cog-91) ([source 1](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/eb90d03740755f5252b8b12cce91fd09970f2d81/cognee/api/v1/cognify/cognify.py#L578-L638); [source 2](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/eb90d03740755f5252b8b12cce91fd09970f2d81/cognee/modules/cognify/config.py#L10-L28)); [AG@72](#e-ag-72) ([source 1](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/observe.ts#L46-L114); [source 2](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/observe.ts#L146-L233)); [RD@41](#e-rd-41) ([source 1](https://github.com/redis/agent-memory-server/blob/94192c39e2a4a154f441a5411e3d73c4f54974a6/V0/agent_memory_server/memory_strategies.py#L539); [source 2](https://github.com/redis/agent-memory-server/blob/94192c39e2a4a154f441a5411e3d73c4f54974a6/V0/agent_memory_server/long_term_memory.py#L657)).

**Open defects / gates:** None applicable identified in the refreshed `found-in-testing` / `ga-blocker` union; absence of a mapped report is not a correctness guarantee.

**Release qualification:** Audited reclassification is implemented but off, SAL-gated and model-dependent. It refines a type label rather than establishing factual truth. No applicable open report identified in the two queried label sets.

**Claim boundary:** This refines stored type metadata; it does not validate factual truth or introduce a separately routed classifier model. Reclassified rows are skipped on rerun, but unchanged Observation candidates remain eligible. The bounded list is fetched before the Observation filter, so eventual progress through every candidate is not established by the budget alone. No directly matching open issue appeared in the two requested label snapshots.

#### 6.3 Open issue register and applicability

These are the 156 distinct open reports returned by the two requested label queries at synthesis time. A facet's mapping is a relevance assessment, not a claim that every issue reproduces on this release. Some open reports have no mapped facet. The labels and exact issue titles below preserve that distinction; facet boundaries explain direct, adjacent and later-code applicability.

Specific scope corrections: #3823's allow-mode plaintext allegation conflicts with the pinned transport floor; #4010/#4018/#4048 concern later containment/internal-only work and do not add those features to this release. #4116's second-connection escalation mechanism has a source-inferred release subset, not every later fix-branch call site. #4117 is a load-sensitive SQLITE_BUSY test failure, not proof of lost counter updates. #4120's macOS/BSD behavior is reported, not reproduced. #4121/#4122 have source-visible release subsets despite later carrier wording. #4124 concerns best-effort recall accounting, not lost memory writes. #3637 is an adversarial-review gate and #3709 an umbrella, not demonstrated cryptographic breaks.

#### 6.4 Comparator source catalog

Each card describes the inspected source, not the entire current hosted product. Facet records decide whether the described behavior is equivalent or merely adjacent. The catalog reproduces the source-backed comparison evidence used by the votes; quoted dossier wording is assessment material, not vendor marketing. SHA-256 checks of the read-only local clones matched the previous source audit. Source pins remain in each URL. Duplicate cards for one product do not count as different competitors.

<a id="e-ag-100"></a>
##### AG@100

**Mesh is implemented.** Peer registration, push/pull/both HTTP sync, shared-scope selection, timestamp deltas and a shared bearer token exist. Default replicated categories: memories, actions, semantic/procedural records, relations and graph nodes/edges. Sync requires `AGENTMEMORY_SECRET`, uses 30-second fetch timeouts, blocks selected private/local URLs and rejects redirects. Peers are processed serially; there is no native gossip/consensus replication in this code. src/functions/mesh.ts:19-65, src/functions/mesh.ts:139-203, src/functions/mesh.ts:227-312.

Source: [agentmemory/src/functions/mesh.ts:19](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/mesh.ts#L19-L65); [agentmemory/src/functions/mesh.ts:139](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/mesh.ts#L139-L203); [agentmemory/src/functions/mesh.ts:227](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/mesh.ts#L227-L312).

<a id="e-ag-136"></a>
##### AG@136

**MCP is first-party.** Full daemon MCP handlers cover tools/resources/prompts; standalone stdio supports multiple protocol versions and proxies to REST where available. The tool registry has a core set of eight, but **code defaults to `all`**, contradicting AGENTS.md's “8 visible by default” statement. The standalone fallback explicitly supports seven tools and announces reduced operation. It should not be confused with the full 54-tool claim. src/mcp/server.ts:45-90, src/mcp/server.ts:1334-1365, src/mcp/server.ts:1620-1655, src/mcp/standalone.ts:16-63, src/mcp/tools-registry.ts:946-978, AGENTS.md:119-126.

##### AG@176

| **Text embeddings for documents and queries** | Provider independently selected by `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`, otherwise key priority. OpenAI default `text-embedding-3-small` and OpenRouter default `openai/text-embedding-3-small` have model/dimension environment overrides. Gemini `gemini-embedding-001` (768d), Voyage `voyage-code-3` (1024d), Cohere `embed-english-v3.0` (1024d) are hardcoded in their adapters. Local `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384d, q8) is hardcoded. Only one text-embedding provider instance, but independent of the generation LLM. src/config.ts:269-281, src/providers/embedding/openai.ts:60-86, src/providers/embedding/openrouter.ts:8-25, src/providers/embedding/gemini.ts:5-16, src/providers/embedding/voyage.ts:7-33, src/providers/embedding/cohere.ts:7-33, src/providers/embedding/local.ts:8-44. | No embedding-provider fallback chain. At runtime, embedding failure skips indexing or degrades hybrid recall to available keyword/graph streams (**fail-open for basic storage/retrieval, closed for that vector**). Dimension guard rejects mismatched vectors. Explicit provider construction can throw on missing credentials, before worker boot, so misconfiguration is not universally graceful. Vectors rank results; no direct authorization or deletion gate. src/functions/search.ts:148-177, src/state/hybrid-search.ts:95-101, src/providers/embedding/index.ts:30-75, src/index.ts:168-198. |

<a id="e-ag-179"></a>
##### AG@179

| **Observation extraction/compression, including observation type/importance fields** | Shared generation LLM; opt-in automatic compression. Structured XML parsing + schema retry; default capture uses deterministic synthetic compression with no model. No dedicated classifier model separate from generation. src/functions/observe.ts:302-330, src/functions/compress.ts:111-164, src/eval/self-correct.ts:1-28. | Unparseable result returns `parse_failed`; provider exceptions return a failure result. The schema retry helper can return the first response after all validation attempts fail; the caller only rechecks parsing, so schema-validity is not a strict final write gate. Successful model text **overwrites the observation key**, so model output affects retained representation. This is fail-closed on unparseable compression, not on every schema error, and not an invariant that original raw content is immutable. src/functions/compress.ts:144-176, src/eval/self-correct.ts:14-27, src/functions/compress.ts:254-265. |

<a id="e-ag-202"></a>
##### AG@202

**Native basic messaging exists.** `mem::signal-send` persists a `Signal` with `from`, optional `to`, non-empty `content`, type, thread/reply IDs, metadata and optional expiry. `signal-read` exposes incoming/outgoing/broadcast messages and stamps direct-message read receipts; `signal-threads` groups conversations. REST exposes POST `/agentmemory/signals/send` and GET `/agentmemory/signals`; MCP exposes `memory_signal_send` / `memory_signal_read`. These are native agentmemory APIs, not evidence of an implementation of Google's A2A protocol. src/functions/signals.ts:7-56, src/functions/signals.ts:60-115, src/functions/signals.ts:119-176, src/triggers/api.ts:2747-2793, src/mcp/server.ts:824-871.

##### AG@70

**Records.** Sessions; raw/compressed observations; versioned memories with six categories (`pattern`, `preference`, `architecture`, `bug`, `workflow`, `fact`); summaries; graph nodes/edges; semantic facts; procedural memories. Observation and memory provenance includes optional agent, project, source-observation/session IDs and `Origin` channel (`user`, `agent`, `tool`, `import`, `shared`). Additional layers include lessons, reflective insights, pinned slots and action-chain crystals. These are typed application records, not a formal belief/assertion logic. src/types.ts:1-175, src/types.ts:403-459, src/types.ts:522-549, src/functions/lessons.ts:119-133, src/functions/reflect.ts:287-304, src/functions/slots.ts:14-97, src/functions/crystallize.ts:54-72.

<a id="e-ag-72"></a>
##### AG@72

**Write path.** `observe` validates the payload, optionally deduplicates, redacts private tags/secret-shaped strings, stamps origin and inherits session agent ID, writes raw state, updates streams/session counts, then performs asynchronous LLM compression or synchronous synthetic compression. Both compression paths replace the same observation key; a separate immutable raw-observation ledger is not established by this code. Direct `remember` saves content without an LLM and then updates indexes best-effort. src/functions/observe.ts:46-114, src/functions/observe.ts:146-233, src/functions/observe.ts:302-339, src/functions/compress.ts:157-176, src/functions/remember.ts:152-212.

<a id="e-ag-74"></a>
##### AG@74

**Versions/conflicts.** Direct saves use BM25 candidate generation and Jaccard token similarity; >0.7 similarity supersedes the first qualifying latest memory, records a parent/version and removes the previous version from indexes. >0.4 can return a near-match advisory. This does not establish logical contradiction or truth. The project guard only engages when both records have projects; **there is no corresponding agent-ID guard in this supersession loop**, despite agent IDs being stamped later. Inference: same-project agents can supersede each other's similar memories through this path. src/functions/remember.ts:71-150, src/functions/remember.ts:152-212.

Source: [agentmemory/src/functions/remember.ts:71](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/remember.ts#L71-L150); [agentmemory/src/functions/remember.ts:152](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/bcf4f0d00d1c71e9221287a4778e4122ce2d7574/src/functions/remember.ts#L152-L212).

<a id="e-ag-76"></a>
##### AG@76

**Consolidation/forgetting.** Consolidation groups important observations by concept, calls the shared LLM, and evolves identically titled memories. A multi-tier pipeline derives semantic facts, procedures and reflective insights. Retention combines exponential age decay with salience/access reinforcement; eviction accepts thresholds, dry-run and bounded counts. TTL and automatic forgetting paths exist. “Contradictions” in auto-forget are high token overlap within concept groups, resolved by marking the older memory non-latest—not semantic negation detection. src/functions/consolidate.ts:79-225, src/functions/consolidation-pipeline.ts:73-128, src/functions/consolidation-pipeline.ts:151-215, src/functions/retention.ts:65-120, src/functions/retention.ts:292-320, src/functions/remember.ts:175-177, src/functions/auto-forget.ts:85-141.

**Temporal scope.** Temporal graph extraction stores `tcommit`, `tvalid`, `tvalidEnd`, reasoning, sentiment, alternatives, confidence and edge versions; old edges are marked non-latest and also copied into history. `asOf` filters both commit time and valid interval against the **same timestamp**. Thus there is a real two-time data representation, but not an independently parameterized “known-at T, valid-at V” bitemporal query interface, nor general bitemporality for all memories. src/functions/temporal-graph.ts:123-145, src/functions/temporal-graph.ts:234-256, src/functions/temporal-graph.ts:277-329.

| Audit/tamper evidence | Optional SHA-256 ledger hashes canonical fields including the previous checksum. Append serialization includes process locks, Postgres advisory locks and transactional sequence allocation. Verification detects checksum/chain breaks, but there is no secret key/signature or independent trusted chain-head anchor in this implementation. **Transactions:** SQLAlchemy supports ordinary SQL transactions; SQLite connections configure WAL/busy handling. Provenance batches commit as one relational transaction. Graph/vector writes are deliberately ordered **graph before vectors** with provenance/rollback metadata to recover partial failure; this is not a distributed ACID transaction across SQL, graph, vector and raw files. A rollback handler deletes failed-run artifacts while preserving earlier-run ownership, and leaves relational rollback metadata if graph/vector deletion fails. cognee/infrastructure/databases/relational/sqlalchemy/SqlAlchemyAdapter.py:119–145; cognee/modules/provenance/storage.py:71–115; cognee/tasks/storage/add_data_points.py:155–205; cognee/tasks/storage/add_data_points.py:317–351; cognee/modules/cognify/rollback.py:127–188; cognee/modules/cognify/rollback.py:279–314.

**Conclusion: MULTI-ROLE-MULTI-PROVIDER.** Embeddings are independently configured; extraction, summarization and query stages each have model/provider/endpoint/key/version overrides. `pipeline_stage` installs these in context variables, so concurrent async work can use distinct configurations. The base LLM is `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` at this exact pin; that source default is not a claim about every Cloud deployment. <a id="e-cog-89"></a>
##### COG@89

**CODE — schema:** `DataPoint` is a Pydantic graph node; scalar fields become properties, DataPoint references become edges, `index_fields` identify per-type/per-field vector collections, and explicit identity fields produce normalized UUID5 IDs. Nodes have creation/update timestamps, version, `valid_to`, ontology URI, pipeline/task/user/content-hash provenance and feedback/importance weights. Typed edges support named relationships, properties and multiple weights. Custom schemas without identity fields get random IDs and therefore do not deduplicate automatically. cognee/infrastructure/engine/models/DataPoint.py:28–106; cognee/infrastructure/engine/models/DataPoint.py:164–193; cognee/infrastructure/engine/models/Edge.py:13–56.

<a id="e-cog-93"></a>
##### COG@93

**Consolidation:** improve's ordered stages apply feedback weights, persist session QA/traces, extract agent context, distill sessions, update preferences, build a truth subspace, enrich triplets and build a global context index. Distillation uses a curator and a writer/judge: accepted lessons become new documents via add+cognify. Failed curator/writer calls leave the watermark unadvanced so work can be retried. This is model-mediated curation, not a formal belief-revision calculus. cognee/modules/improve/registry.py:27–37; cognee/modules/session_distillation/distill.py:213–234; cognee/modules/session_distillation/distill.py:378–435; cognee/modules/session_distillation/distill.py:499–528.

`remember` resolves missing scope/category/importance through the configured LLM, embeds content, finds similar records, and applies consolidation plans. Batch encoding includes near-duplicate elimination; defaults include a 0.98 intra-batch similarity threshold and 0.85 consolidation threshold. **CODE:** shallow recall embeds a query and performs one vector search. Deep recall uses `RecallFlow`: query analysis, selected scopes, parallel searches, a confidence/budget router, and optional deeper LLM exploration. Short queries can skip query-analysis inference; deep recall still constructs the configured LLM. It is not a demonstrated universally superior retrieval algorithm. lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/unified_memory.py:739 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/recall_flow.py:181 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/recall_flow.py:274
Default composite weights are **0.5 semantic + 0.3 recency + 0.2 importance**, with a 30-day recency half-life based on `created_at`. This is a relevance score, not a calibrated probability of truth. LanceDB converts its returned distance to `1/(1+distance)`; the wrapper does not establish that every backend's score has identical meaning. lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/types.py:144 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/types.py:345 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/storage/lancedb_storage.py:405
Scope filters run in the vector query, categories/metadata are post-filtered with finite oversampling, and private-record filtering is in the memory recall layer. Thus filtered queries can underfill requested `limit`. Storage exceptions inside deep recall are caught per search and skipped, potentially producing incomplete or empty results rather than a hard failure. lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/storage/lancedb_storage.py:373 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/unified_memory.py:751 lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/recall_flow.py:97

**5. Memory model and temporal semantics.** Graphiti's primary memory objects are episodes, entities, fact edges, communities, and sagas. Episodes hold raw source content, a source type/description, occurrence time, and source metadata. Entity nodes hold name embeddings, summaries, and typed attributes. Fact edges contain the relation, fact text, embedding, contributing episode IDs, `created_at`, `valid_at`, `invalid_at`, `expired_at`, and `reference_time`. This explicitly separates real-world validity from system observation/invalidation. Communities summarize clusters; saga state includes ordered-episode pointers and summary watermarks. <a id="e-hn-50"></a>
##### HN@50

**Honcho's distinctive implementation is social/perspective memory.** Workspaces contain peers and sessions; membership has join/leave timestamps. A collection is keyed by **workspace + observer + observed**. Documents store conclusions, a level, derivation count, embedding, optional session association, deletion timestamp and source linkage. This explicitly represents “what agent A knows about B,” alongside self-representations, rather than relying only on generic namespace conventions. Dream specialists perform deduction and induction, can update peer cards, and can create/delete observations. Peer cards are concise identity artifacts; they are unrelated to A2A protocol Agent Cards. Model-derived assertions remain fallible inferences. **Document memory:** `Document` provides ID, text/blob, arbitrary metadata, score, dense and sparse embeddings. <a id="e-hs-76"></a>
##### HS@76

**Consolidation and forgetting:** core has real context compaction, not just recipes. `CompactionHook` triggers at a configurable context-window fraction and rewrites the live message list. Strategies include sliding-window removal, pruning old tool results, and an LLM summarizer. The summarizer proceeds through historical turns, historical summaries, current-task steps and current-task summaries while protecting a minimum context floor; it checks that the result shrinks, not that it is factually faithful. These are lossy working-context transformations, with no durable source archive implied. <a id="e-hs-80"></a>
##### HS@80

**Provenance:** document splitting preserves source IDs and split positions; Mem0 recall retains backend memory IDs, entity IDs, scores and creation/update timestamps under `meta['mem0']`. Cognee recall renders selected response text into a system message without preserving the returned object's structured provenance. Neither wrapper signs the originating writer identity. **Consistency:** tool execution builds batches from State read/write dependencies; cycles break deterministically by call order, and results merge in call order. This is deterministic local scheduling, not distributed consensus, durable synchronization or CRDT convergence. `shared=True` in the in-memory document store shares dictionaries only inside one process. **Critical layer distinction:** underlying AndaDB offers BM25, HNSW and RRF (`k=60` default). **The assessed Rust KIP Nexus exposes keyword/BM25 search only**; non-keyword modes return `SearchModeUnsupported`. <a id="e-lg-40"></a>
##### LG@40

LangMem's core is Python. Memory tools produce LangChain `StructuredTool` objects; extraction uses chat models and `trustcall.create_extractor`; persistent operations delegate to LangGraph's `BaseStore`. The memory-store manager retrieves candidates, proposes structured memory changes, optionally performs additional consolidation/enrichment phases, then calls store puts/deletes. It is not itself a new database, replication protocol or self-contained daemon. LangGraph deliberately separates **checkpoint persistence for graph execution** from **Store persistence across threads**. `StateGraph.compile` accepts both a checkpointer and a Store. Checkpoints preserve channel values, channel versions, versions seen and parent relationships; Store records use namespaces and keys. **CODE:** the vector memory block computes a query embedding from recent messages, requests top-k matches (default two), applies session metadata filters, and runs optional node postprocessors. Query parameters and embedding objects are independently injectable. It requires a vector store that stores text. llama-index-core/llama_index/core/memory/memory_blocks/vector.py:40 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/memory/memory_blocks/vector.py:67 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/memory/memory_blocks/vector.py:100
The broader framework goes further: `QueryFusionRetriever` accepts multiple retrievers and an independent query-generation LLM; it implements reciprocal-rank, relative-score, distance-based and simple fusion modes. `PropertyGraphIndex` accepts graph extractors, graph/vector stores and separately chosen embedding/LLM components; `LLMRerank` independently accepts its judging LLM. These are concrete extensibility advantages over a fixed memory-recall pipeline. They are **not all enabled by default inside `VectorMemoryBlock`**. llama-index-core/llama_index/core/retrievers/fusion_retriever.py:24 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/retrievers/fusion_retriever.py:113 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/indices/property_graph/base.py:80 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/postprocessor/llm_rerank.py:36
**Isolation qualification:** a reused vector block mutates `query_kwargs` to insert a session filter and then preserves an existing session filter without checking its value. Session A followed by B can still query A. This is a demonstrated same-object reuse hazard, not a claim that separately constructed per-session blocks always leak. The host application must establish authorization independently of metadata filtering. llama-index-core/llama_index/core/memory/memory_blocks/vector.py:123
**CODE:** `AgentWorkflow` manages named agents, per-agent tools, dynamic tool retrieval, shared context/memory, routing and handoffs. `can_handoff_to` is checked by the actual handoff function, not only prompt text. Events dispatch tool calls and collect results; each agent has its own LLM. LlamaIndex therefore supplies considerably more of the **agent application execution loop** than an endpoint memory substrate. llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/multi_agent_workflow.py:73 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/multi_agent_workflow.py:248 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/multi_agent_workflow.py:632 llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/base_agent.py:94

<a id="e-mo-46"></a>
##### MO@46

**CODE:** memories are UUID-addressed text payloads, hash, timestamps and metadata, scoped through `user_id`, `agent_id` and/or `run_id`. Expiration is represented and filtered in list/search; it is not evidence of physical erasure from history, backups or logs. A procedural-memory path remains for agent-scoped summaries; arbitrary typed memory kinds are rejected by this API. mem0/configs/base.py:16 mem0/memory/main.py:760 mem0/memory/main.py:817 mem0/memory/main.py:831 mem0/memory/main.py:1680
**The current inference path is ADD-only.** It retrieves context, makes one extraction call, embeds proposed memories, deduplicates hashes against its retrieved/batch sets, and inserts. Explicit `update`/`delete` APIs remain; the `add` docstring's claim that the model chooses add/update/delete is stale relative to the implementation. This is a concrete advantage over a destructive automatic consolidation path: ingestion does not let extraction output silently replace/delete existing records. It does not prevent bad new facts, incomplete extraction or accumulation of contradictory records. `infer=False` writes supplied messages without fact extraction. mem0/memory/main.py:881 mem0/memory/main.py:942 mem0/memory/main.py:1015 mem0/memory/main.py:1208 mem0/memory/main.py:2052 mem0/memory/main.py:2114
**CODE:** query lemmatization and entity extraction precede embedding; vector search overfetches `max(limit*4,60)`. A separate keyword query produces normalized BM25 values, entity matching supplies boosts, and additive scoring normalizes the active signals. An optional reranker runs when configured and requested; its failure falls back to original results. Current default `rerank` is false. mem0/memory/main.py:1393 mem0/memory/main.py:1507 mem0/memory/main.py:1642 mem0/utils/scoring.py:57
**Important limit:** the candidate set is built from **semantic results only**. Keyword/entity matches score those candidates; they do not independently inject otherwise absent memories into that set. A semantic threshold is applied before hybrid scoring, so keyword/entity strength cannot rescue an excluded candidate. spaCy/model availability and backend keyword support affect which signals are active. This is stronger than describing Mem0 as only cosine search, but weaker than claiming a full lexical/vector union or equivalent hybrid behavior across all providers. mem0/memory/main.py:1660 mem0/memory/main.py:1680 mem0/utils/scoring.py:103 mem0/utils/spacy_models.py:44

##### MO@54

**CODE:** query lemmatization and entity extraction precede embedding; vector search overfetches `max(limit*4,60)`. A separate keyword query produces normalized BM25 values, entity matching supplies boosts, and additive scoring normalizes the active signals. An optional reranker runs when configured and requested; its failure falls back to original results. Current default `rerank` is false. mem0/memory/main.py:1393 mem0/memory/main.py:1507 mem0/memory/main.py:1642 mem0/utils/scoring.py:57
**Important limit:** the candidate set is built from **semantic results only**. Keyword/entity matches score those candidates; they do not independently inject otherwise absent memories into that set. A semantic threshold is applied before hybrid scoring, so keyword/entity strength cannot rescue an excluded candidate. spaCy/model availability and backend keyword support affect which signals are active. This is stronger than describing Mem0 as only cosine search, but weaker than claiming a full lexical/vector union or equivalent hybrid behavior across all providers. mem0/memory/main.py:1660 mem0/memory/main.py:1680 mem0/utils/scoring.py:103 mem0/utils/spacy_models.py:44

<a id="e-mp-181"></a>
##### MP@181

There is no single mandatory generation model. Embedding configuration is independent of generation configuration; initialization/rooms/KG use an explicit provider object, closet regeneration has separate endpoint/model variables, and benchmark rerankers have their own settings. An operator can combine local MiniLM/EmbeddingGemma or a remote embedding API with an Ollama or Anthropic classifier and another OpenAI-compatible closet model. This is configuration separation, not automatic concurrent provider failover or a router that optimizes models per request. mempalace/embedding.py:739–811, mempalace/llm_client.py:530–554, mempalace/closet_llm.py:95–123, benchmarks/longmemeval_bench.py:2770–2798.

<a id="e-mp-205"></a>
##### MP@205

**Native messaging exists.** `logstream.sqlite3` stores immutable events and exact UTF-8 artifacts. Events include type, stream, room, topic, from/to-agent, correlation ID, branch/base commit, status, body, metadata and replica ordering. MCP provides append/list/wait/ack, task creation and patch/artifact operations; CLI provides inbox-style watch and explicit task launch. This is a persistent shared blackboard/event bus, not merely shared retrieval. mempalace/logstream.py:492–540, mempalace/mcp_server/tools_coord.py:14–80, mempalace/logstream.py:864–945, mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:189–199, mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:590–657.
| Transport | MCP stdio/HTTP tools; HTTP `/logstream/stream` SSE; peer anti-entropy via HTTP(S) bearer requests. Native SQLite persistence avoids a required external broker. mempalace/mcp_server/_guards.py:33–48, mempalace/mcp_server/http.py:407–417, mempalace/logsync.py:51–101. |
| Wake mechanism | `wait_events` blocks one request; `logstream watch` persists cursors and can exit 0 on a matching event, 2 on idle timeout, allowing a harness to wake the agent. SSE streams live events with resume cursors. This wakes an already listening consumer; it is not a proven autonomous scheduler that boots sleeping hosts or starts all agents on delivery. mempalace/logstream.py:1087–1122, mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:189–209, mempalace/mcp_server/http.py:832–845. |
| Agent launch / external orchestration | Explicit task run adapters can launch installed Codex/Claude CLIs after checking recipient/runner identity and workspace. They use a subprocess argument list, not an interpolated shell command. External agent executables and their lifecycle remain necessary. mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:497–509, mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:590–657. |
| Content versus signalling | **Content-bearing**, not content-free: SSE sends the same full event envelope as event listing; event body and metadata are stored. Large exact patches/files are fetched as artifacts by ID; artifact content is UTF-8 text, not an arbitrary binary blob facility. mempalace/logstream.py:796–825, mempalace/logstream.py:948–969, mempalace/mcp_server/http.py:915–925. |

##### MP@69

**Primary memories** are text drawers: content plus wing, room, source path, chunk index, adding agent, filing time and normalization/ID recipe. Optional source line ranges, content date with its extraction provenance, source mtime/inode and expected chunk count support traceability and resumable ingestion. Closets are a separate compact index pointing to drawers; they are not the authoritative original text. mempalace/miner.py:1731–1808, mempalace/miner.py:2037–2076, mempalace/closet_llm.py:192–203.

##### MP@71

**Graph:** entities have name/type/properties; triples carry subject/predicate/object, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, confidence, source closet/file/drawer, adapter and extraction timestamp. It supports temporal as-of queries and atomic fact supersession with a shared half-open boundary. This is valid-time history plus extraction provenance, **not verified full bitemporal transaction-history querying**, and not a first-class competing-belief/assertion calculus. mempalace/knowledge_graph.py:111–139, mempalace/knowledge_graph.py:160–183, mempalace/knowledge_graph.py:375–408.

**Consolidation/forgetting:** optional LLM closet regeneration creates topics, quotes and a brief summary only in the index layer, preserving drawer documents in that path. **CODE:** the basic unit is a Markdown chunk with content, source path, nearest heading, heading level and start/end line positions. <a id="e-ms-49"></a>
##### MS@49

Indexing is incremental: unchanged chunks avoid embedding calls; obsolete chunk IDs are deleted; directory-root cleanup prunes deleted sources only inside the current run's roots. Errors are accumulated per file in `IndexReport`. **Limitation:** stale chunks are deleted before replacement embeddings are computed, so an embedding failure can leave the index missing the old version. The Markdown original remains available for recovery; this is index inconsistency, not demonstrated source-data destruction. src/memsearch/core.py:112 src/memsearch/core.py:178 src/memsearch/core.py:202

**Code:** Rust path locks serialize filesystem work; Python's `transaction` package explicitly says lock management moved to RAGFS. Queue delivery distinguishes completed/cancelled work from exceptions left unacknowledged. Memory writes, deletes, link migration and vectorization are separate steps with per-operation errors. <a id="e-ox-61"></a>
##### OX@61

Git is the collaboration transport for shared artifacts. Murmurs can be queued locally when the daemon is unavailable; after Git pulls, a relay inserts new remote messages into the whisper registry and persists deduplication state. This is **team/repo synchronization and coordination**, with store-and-forward behavior. **V0 — CODE.** Two tiers are implemented. `WorkingMemory` holds ordered messages, structured memories for promotion, arbitrary JSON data, a context summary, session/user/namespace identifiers and an extraction strategy. Its TTL is optional and defaults to persistence. The write path stores native Redis JSON and applies expiration separately. Long-term records carry text, semantic/episodic/message type, user/session/namespace, creation/update/access timestamps, access count, pinning, topics, entities, deduplication hash, extraction provenance, event date and metadata. ##### TC@114

Profile synchronization compares MD5/baseline versions and calls a store sync interface; TCVDB skips changes whose baseline version has advanced remotely; skill updates use expected-version checks. These are synchronization/concurrency mechanisms within the product, not CRDT convergence or authenticated federation between independently governed memory servers. No peer federation protocol, CRDT implementation or cross-instance trust negotiation was found in the inspected public tree. **Transactions:** SQLite enables WAL and wraps metadata/vector writes in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transactions. A crash or failed replacement after deletion can leave the indexed old memory gone; JSONL may still retain material for recovery. **CODE:** L0 stores original messages, roles, timestamps and session/tenant identifiers. L1 types include `persona`, `episodic`, `instruction`, `work_fact`, `work_task`, `work_method`, and `work_artifact`. Records carry priority, scene, source-message IDs, timestamps, version and session identity. L2 consolidates scenario Markdown; L3 generates a persona file. These are generated textual representations, not a general belief/assertion calculus. MemoryCore/src/core/store/types.ts:140–162 MemoryCore/src/core/record/l1-writer.ts:30–98 MemoryCore/src/core/scene/scene-extractor.ts:252–304 MemoryCore/src/core/persona/persona-generator.ts:198–241
**Write path:** Capture reads the session cursor, records L0 and advances the cursor under a lock; SQLite immediately stores metadata/FTS and schedules embedding work in the background. Subsequent extraction calls an LLM, recalls possible duplicates and obtains `store/update/merge/skip` decisions. Writer appends JSONL and updates indexed records. L2/L3 have their own asynchronous runners. **Consolidation and contradiction:** L1 performs candidate retrieval followed by a batch LLM judgment. Failure defaults to storing all new memories, so contradictory or duplicate memories can coexist after a judge outage. Update/merge deletes indexed targets and creates a replacement; append-only JSONL retains older versions until cleanup. Candidate recall is documented and wired as session-scoped, so this is not a complete cross-session contradiction resolver. <a id="e-tc-90"></a>
##### TC@90

**Write path:** Capture reads the session cursor, records L0 and advances the cursor under a lock; SQLite immediately stores metadata/FTS and schedules embedding work in the background. Subsequent extraction calls an LLM, recalls possible duplicates and obtains `store/update/merge/skip` decisions. Writer appends JSONL and updates indexed records. L2/L3 have their own asynchronous runners. <a id="e-tc-92"></a>
##### TC@92

**Consolidation and contradiction:** L1 performs candidate retrieval followed by a batch LLM judgment. Failure defaults to storing all new memories, so contradictory or duplicate memories can coexist after a judge outage. Update/merge deletes indexed targets and creates a replacement; append-only JSONL retains older versions until cleanup. Candidate recall is documented and wired as session-scoped, so this is not a complete cross-session contradiction resolver. Vestige is a Rust workspace with `vestige-core`, `vestige-mcp`, a separate `vestige-spacetime` crate and test crates. The shipped binary declarations include `vestige-mcp`, `vestige`, and `vestige-restore`. Persistent endpoint storage is SQLite; the MCP crate directly selects the bundled-SQLite core. Search adds local embeddings and USearch; an embedded SvelteKit build supplies the dashboard. These are source-level deployment components, not a managed inference API. A configured floor at or above 1 disables abstention. The HyDE-named module constructs query templates and embedding centroids; it is not evidence of an independent hypothetical-document LLM. <a id="e-v-62"></a>
##### V@62

**Vestige implements shared use, not a verified peer federation mesh.** HTTP sessions each own MCP initialization state but share Storage, CognitiveEngine and event bus; the server uses one bearer token, a 100-session limit and a 50-request concurrency limit. Concurrent stdio has 16 in-flight handlers and bounded pending/writer queues. Those bounds do not establish performance at those counts or isolation between mutually distrustful agents. <a id="e-v-83"></a>
##### V@83

**Vestige does have cryptographic audit evidence.** Its receipt-attestation module uses Ed25519, canonical JSON/DSSE, chain links, salted evidence commitments and separable disclosure mappings. A signed receipt and chain advancement can be persisted atomically with a replay capsule. Public keys have registration/status handling; live retrieval signing requires an explicitly provisioned seed matching the registered active public key. This is substantially stronger than an ordinary mutable event log and must not be scored “no signed audit.” V crates/vestige-core/src/storage/receipt_attestation.rs:1-39 V crates/vestige-core/src/storage/attestation_store.rs:414-538 V crates/vestige-mcp/src/trace_recorder.rs:865-903 V crates/vestige-mcp/src/trace_recorder.rs:1037-1087

##### V@9001

Vestige encryption feature enables bundled SQLCipher. configure_connection reads VESTIGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY and applies PRAGMA key only if nonempty. Optional database encryption, without the same fail-closed requested-selection contract.
